_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for Nepal covering ancient Kirat dynasty, Licchavi era, medieval Malla kingdoms (Kathmandu/Patan/Bhaktapur), Prithvi Narayan Shah's unification 1768, Gorkha expansionism, Anglo-Nepalese War 1814-16 (Gurkha reputation), Rana oligarchy 1846-1951, monarchy restoration, Panchayat system, Maoist insurgency 1996-2006, royal massacre 2001, abolition of monarchy 2008, federal democratic republic, earthquakes, and India-China geopolitical balancing.

religion.note: Hindu-Buddhist syncretism common; Pashupatinath (holiest Hindu temple); Lumbini (Buddha's birthplace, UNESCO); formerly only Hindu kingdom globally (until 2006 secular declaration); caste system legally abolished but socially persistent

ethnic_groups.name: Chhettri (Kshatriya)
ethnic_groups.notes: Hill Hindu warrior caste; Indo-Aryan; politically dominant; Nepali-speaking; Prithvi Narayan Shah was Chhettri; ruling elite

ethnic_groups.name: Brahmin (Hill and Terai)
ethnic_groups.notes: Hindu priestly caste; Indo-Aryan; educated elite; disproportionate political power; Bahun (hill Brahmin) vs Madhesi Brahmin

ethnic_groups.name: Magar
ethnic_groups.notes: Tibeto-Burman; hill people; historically martial (Gurkhas); shamanic traditions; Nepal's largest indigenous group

ethnic_groups.name: Tharu
ethnic_groups.notes: Terai (lowland plains); indigenous; farming; bonded labour (Kamaiya system) abolished 2000; jungle specialists

ethnic_groups.name: Tamang
ethnic_groups.notes: Tibeto-Burman; Kathmandu valley hills; Buddhist; close to Tibetan culture; historically marginalised

ethnic_groups.name: Newar
ethnic_groups.notes: Indigenous to Kathmandu valley; Malla kingdom heirs; Tibeto-Burman language; urban; merchants; Buddhism-Hinduism syncretic; Newari architecture; festivals (Indra Jatra)

ethnic_groups.name: Kami (Dalit)
ethnic_groups.notes: Blacksmiths; 'untouchable' Dalit caste; discrimination persists despite legal equality; poorest

ethnic_groups.name: Muslim (Madhesi and Pahari)
ethnic_groups.notes: Terai Muslims; cross-border with India; Urdu/Maithili; some hill Muslims

ethnic_groups.name: Yadav (Madhesi)
ethnic_groups.notes: Terai plains; culturally close to Bihar (India); Maithili language; Hindu; farming

ethnic_groups.name: Rai, Gurung, Limbu, Sherpa, Other
ethnic_groups.notes: Numerous Tibeto-Burman hill tribes; Sherpa (Solu-Khumbu, Buddhist, mountaineering); Gurung (Gurkhas); Rai/Limbu (Kirat); 125 ethnic groups, 123 languages; great diversity

independence.from: United Kingdom recognised independence in treaty 1923; unified by Prithvi Narayan Shah 1768

country_profile.notes_unique: Only country with non-rectangular flag; home to Mount Everest (Sagarmatha, 8,849m); never colonised; Gurkha soldiers famous globally (British/Indian armies); 2001 royal massacre (Crown Prince Dipendra killed family); 2015 earthquake killed 9,000; Maoist insurgency (1996-2006, ~17,000 dead); abolished monarchy 2008; remittances ~25% GDP (Gulf workers); Lumbini (Buddha's birthplace)

trade.notes: Massive trade deficit offset by remittances; India dominant trade partner (65%+ imports); landlocked logistics challenge; carpet/pashmina traditional exports; hydropower export potential.

infrastructure.notes: Mountain terrain extreme infrastructure challenge; Tribhuvan Airport only international; Pokhara International Airport (2023); hydropower surplus emerging; Indian railway connection planned.

governance_indices.notes: Federal democratic republic (abolished monarchy 2008); 7 provinces; coalition politics unstable; Maoist integration complete; caste-based discrimination persisting.

country_profile.national_motto: Mother and Motherland are greater than heaven
country_profile.national_anthem: Sayaun Thunga Phulka (Made of Hundreds of Flowers)

geography.terrain: Terai plains south; hills mid-zone; Himalayas north including 8 of world's 14 peaks above 8000m
geography.notes: Home to Mount Everest; 8 of 14 eight-thousanders; buffer between India and China; seismically active (2015 earthquake 9,000+ killed); Hindu-majority with Buddhist heritage.

economy_extended.notes: Remittance-dependent (25%+ GDP); hydropower potential (83 GW, <3% developed); tourism (Everest, Lumbini); landlocked between India/China; currency pegged to INR.

health.notes: Low hospital bed density; mountain terrain limits access; female community health volunteers effective; high stunting; earthquake-damaged infrastructure; medical tourism to India.

food_agriculture.notes: Terai breadbasket; subsistence farming dominant; largest cardamom producer globally; Darjeeling-type tea; food insecurity in remote mountains; post-earthquake agricultural recovery.

security_stability.border_disputes: Kalapani/Lipulekh with India; historical border issues
security_stability.notes: Post-civil war stability; federal republic since 2015; Gurkha soldiers renowned globally; India-China buffer; UN peacekeeping major contributor; Bhutanese refugee resettlement.

environment_climate.notes: Glacial lake outburst flood (GLOF) risk; Everest region glacial retreat; community forestry success story; snow leopard habitat; Kathmandu Valley air pollution severe.

demographics_extended.notes: Multi-ethnic (125+ groups); Khas-Arya dominant; Tharu, Magar, Tamang, Newar significant; caste system persisting; massive labor migration (Gulf, Malaysia, Korea).

comparative_rankings._note: Country position relative to continent and global.
comparative_rankings.notes: Home of Mt. Everest; federal democratic republic since 2008; remittance-dependent economy; birthplace of Buddha.

cultural_heritage.national_animal: cow (national animal); Danphe (national bird, Himalayan monal)
cultural_heritage.national_sport: Volleyball (national sport); cricket and football popular
cultural_heritage.media_landscape: Kantipur Daily (Nepali); Kathmandu Post, Republica (English); NTV; relatively free press.
cultural_heritage.notes: Only Hindu kingdom until 2008; Newari architecture; Lumbini (Buddha's birthplace); Gurkha warrior tradition; Mt. Everest; trekking capital.

energy.notes: Massive untapped hydropower potential (83,000 MW theoretical); Upper Tamakoshi (456 MW) largest; exports surplus to India; still imports petroleum from India.

human_rights_gender.notes: First Asian country to recognise third gender (2007); LGBTQ rights pioneer in South Asia; caste-based discrimination persists; Madhesi rights; child marriage challenge.

legal_system.legal_tradition: Common law and Hindu legal tradition; statutory law
legal_system.customary_law_role: Caste and indigenous customary law in rural areas
legal_system.notes: Federal constitution since 2015 (7 provinces); Supreme Court; transitional justice from Maoist conflict (1996–2006) incomplete; new civil and criminal codes (2018).

tourism.notes: Trekking capital of the world; Everest summit expeditions; spiritual/yoga tourism; 2015 earthquake recovery; Visit Nepal campaigns.

transport.notes: Extreme terrain challenges; Lukla Airport iconic; cross-border railway from India expanding; road network fragile (landslides); no major railway system.

910.name: Ancient Nepal and Kirata Period
910.description: The earliest settlements in the Kathmandu Valley, the legendary Kirata dynasty, the birth of Siddhartha Gautama (the Buddha) in Lumbini, and the region's connections to the Maurya Empire.

sub_clusters.name: Prehistoric Kathmandu Valley
sub_clusters.description: The geological legend of the Kathmandu Valley as a drained lake, early Neolithic settlements, the Kirata tribal kingdoms, and the valley's development as a fertile agricultural center.

920.name: Medieval Malla Kingdoms
920.description: The Malla dynasty's remarkable rule of the Kathmandu Valley, the three rival kingdoms of Kathmandu, Patan, and Bhaktapur, their extraordinary architectural competition, and the Newari cultural zenith.
